subtopics.title: Models, Metrics, Notation & Key Facts
subtopics.subtitle: Process models, design orderings, test techniques, COCOMO, CMMI, UML and patterns

concepts.text: Software engineering and OOAD questions test a compact set of orderings, model names, notation symbols and a handful of metrics. The tables below collect them in syllabus order, from process models to exception handling. Use this sheet for last-minute revision; each entry is explained with examples in its own subtopic.

rows: each dev phase paired with a test level
deliver or refine the system in slices

items: Functional requirements say what the system does; non-functional requirements constrain how well (performance, security, usability, reliability).
NFR classes (Sommerville): product, organisational and external requirements.
RE process: feasibility study → elicitation and analysis → specification (SRS) → validation, with requirements management throughout.
Good SRS (IEEE 830): correct, unambiguous, complete, consistent, ranked, verifiable, modifiable and traceable.
Verification: are we building the product right? Validation: are we building the right product?

rows: data, stamp, control, external, common, content
functional, sequential, communicational, procedural, temporal, logical, coincidental

items: Organisation styles: repository (shared data), client–server, layered, pipe-and-filter, MVC, broker, peer-to-peer.
Centralised control: call–return (top-down subroutines) or manager model (one process coordinates others).
Event-based control: broadcast (events sent to all subscribed components) or interrupt-driven (handlers for real-time events).
Client–server tiers: two-tier thin client (logic on server) vs fat client (logic on client); three-tier separates presentation, application and data.
CBSE: components expose provides and requires interfaces and are composed sequentially, hierarchically or additively.

rows: at developer site vs at user site

concepts.plainText: Cyclomatic complexity: edges − nodes + 2 × components = decision points + 1
Basic COCOMO: effort in person-months, duration in months, average staff

items: A baseline is a formally reviewed work product that changes only through change control.
Change requests are assessed by a change control board (CCB) for cost, impact and priority.
Version management tracks versions and branches; semantic versioning MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH bumps MAJOR for incompatible changes.
Release management packages executables, data, documentation and installation instructions for customers.
Use cases (brief, casual, fully dressed) → domain model (conceptual classes, associations, attributes) → system sequence diagrams and operation contracts.
Design: interaction diagrams assign responsibilities using GRASP; design class diagrams add methods, navigability and visibility.
GRASP: information expert, creator, controller, low coupling, high cohesion, polymorphism, pure fabrication, indirection, protected variations.
Visibility from A to B: attribute, parameter, local or global.
Implementation: map DCD attributes to fields, multiplicity * to collections, create messages to constructors; code least-coupled classes first.

rows: Singleton, Factory Method, Abstract Factory, Builder, Prototype
Adapter, Composite, Decorator, Facade, Proxy, Bridge, Flyweight
Observer, Strategy, Command, Iterator, Template Method, State

items: try holds risky code, catch handles a matching exception, finally always runs, throw raises and throws declares.
Java checked exceptions (IOException) must be caught or declared; unchecked ones (RuntimeException subclasses) need not be.
An uncaught exception propagates up the call stack until a matching handler is found or the program ends.

notes.text: Numeric questions here are mostly: cyclomatic complexity from a flow graph, COCOMO effort and duration, function points, DRE, availability, communication paths and boundary-value test counts. Write the formula first, then substitute.

Easy swaps: aggregation (hollow) vs composition (filled) diamond; <<include>> (always runs) vs <<extend>> (conditional); verification vs validation; alpha (developer site) vs beta (user site); stub (replaces a called module) vs driver (calls the module under test).
Orderings are frequent MCQ material: coupling data → content, cohesion functional → coincidental, and CMMI Initial → Managed → Defined → Quantitatively Managed → Optimizing.

formulas.title: Cyclomatic complexity
formulas.description: E edges, N nodes and P connected components of the control-flow graph; equals the number of independent paths.

formulas.title: Basic COCOMO
formulas.description: Effort in person-months and duration in months, with constants chosen by organic, semi-detached or embedded mode.

formulas.title: Adjusted function points
formulas.description: The 14 general system characteristics Fi, each rated 0–5, adjust the unadjusted count by ±35%.

formulas.title: Defect removal efficiency
formulas.description: E errors found before delivery and D defects found after delivery.

formulas.title: Availability
formulas.description: MTTF + MTTR is the mean time between failures; availability is the fraction of time the system is up.

flashcards.front: Order the types of coupling from best to worst.
flashcards.back: Data, stamp, control, external, common, content coupling.

flashcards.front: Name the five CMMI maturity levels in order.
flashcards.back: Initial, Managed, Defined, Quantitatively Managed, Optimizing.

flashcards.front: What do the UML visibility markers +, −, # and ~ mean?
flashcards.back: Public, private, protected and package visibility.

flashcards.front: What is the difference between a stub and a driver?
flashcards.back: A stub stands in for a module that the unit under test calls (top-down integration); a driver calls the unit under test (bottom-up integration).

questions.questionText: Using basic COCOMO in organic mode (a = 2.4, b = 1.05), the effort for a 32 KLOC project is approximately:
Basic COCOMO in semi-detached mode uses a = 3.0 and b = 1.12. The effort for a 50 KLOC project is approximately:
questions.explanation: E = 3.0 × 50^1.12 ≈ 3.0 × 79.96 ≈ 240 person-months; organic constants would give about 146 and embedded about 394.

questions.questionText: At which CMMI maturity level does an organisation first control its processes using statistical and other quantitative techniques?
questions.explanation: Level 4 adds quantitative process management; level 5 then uses that data for continuous improvement.

questions.questionText: Which GRASP pattern assigns the responsibility for receiving and handling a system event to a non-UI class that represents the overall system or a use-case scenario?
questions.explanation: Controller is the first object beyond the UI layer that receives system operations, such as a Register or ProcessSaleHandler.

questions.questionText: An existing class offers the right functionality but through an incompatible interface. Which GoF pattern wraps it so that clients can use the interface they expect?
questions.explanation: Adapter converts one interface into another; Facade simplifies a whole subsystem, Decorator adds behaviour and Proxy controls access with the same interface.
